fields.statement: Verifier claude-code-3458be59 at bd4bc087 (attempt 2, after review cycle 1). Read the diff: blockedNotice.notify now remembers state=blocked, the kind only when rexRecord writes it (permission/question/auth), and rexField(rexNoticeMsg(n), rexMsgMax), the same msg rexRecord encodes, so a multi-line or over-long question's echo matches and is skipped (quality f1). Ran go test ./cmd/rhiza -count=1 -run TestScripts/(headless-run-blocked-notice|session-run-blocked-notice|run-blocked|headless-run-agent-tabs)$: all PASS. headless-run-blocked-notice drives rhiza run start --foreground with REX_BLOCK empty under a fake rex and claude: each agent pane holds exactly one state=blocked:kind=permission:app=rhiza:title= report and the driver's output holds no 7501 or state= report (compliance f1). session-run-blocked-notice covers, with the agent's blocked report, the wrapper's echo and the agent's working report: one root-record blocked report with app=rhiza and kind/title/msg naming change set, step and tab, no working report; the record's Rex status is the agent's blocked report and message while blocked and working: Back to work after; the same for a question in a non-autonomous run and a new multi-line question case; an autonomous question writes no report while a permission block does. run-blocked still passes for --foreground with REX_BLOCK. Full go test ./cmd/rhiza -count=1: ok. go vet ./...: ok; gofmt -l: clean. go test ./internal/api fails only TestReadBudget (timing medians ~50-60ms under load average ~9); the diff does not touch the read path. Gaps: the session record is checked through session show's '- rex:' text lines, not --json (compliance f2, minor); the headless script's events stream gives no echo, the echo being exercised in session-run-blocked-notice instead.
